The presidential candidate of the Nigeria Democratic Congress, Peter Obi, has demanded a thorough investigation into the killing of four party supporters during a political gathering in Delta State. Obi, who condemned the attack as a senseless act of violence, called on security agencies to identify and prosecute those responsible, including any sponsors. In a statement on Tuesday, the former Anambra State governor said 15 other supporters sustained serious injuries in the attack in Uduere, Ughelli North Local Government Area. He identified the deceased as Moses Anaughe, a former Federal Commissioner of the Federal Character Commission; Akima Efenena Umukoro, a former President of the Urhobo Progress Union Youth Wing; and Nyoren Okoro, an NDC chieftain. He said the identity of the fourth victim had yet to be established. Among those injured were Evance Ivwurie, Chairman of Senator Ovie Omo-Agege’s Campaign Organisation, and Chuks Erhire, its Director-General. Make PUNCH part of your everyday experience. Add us to your Preferred Sources Obi, who expressed condolences to the families of the deceased, said, “I offer my deepest condolences to the families of those who died and pray for a swift recovery for the injured.” He urged security agencies to “conduct a comprehensive investigation, identify those responsible and their sponsors, and ensure they face justice.” The former governor also called on the authorities to take immediate steps to protect Nigerians participating in political activities. He said, “Every Nigerian has a constitutional right to support any political party or candidate without fear of intimidation or violence.” Delta killings: Impunity fuelling political violence – Falana NDC denies rift with Obi over campaign funding Four killed as gunmen attack Omo-Agege’s campaign convoy Expressing concern over the escalation of political hostility, Obi said it was no longer enough for those behind attacks on opposition supporters to spread false claims against them. “It is no longer sufficient for those responsible to fund the dissemination of false claims against the opposition. They have now escalated to the appalling practice of murdering innocent Nigerians solely because of their political affiliations. This is completely unacceptable,” he said. He added that political disagreements should not result in violence, insisting that elections and persuasion remained the legitimate ways to resolve political differences. “Political differences must be resolved through persuasion and the ballot, never through the use of bullets. No political ambition is worth the life of even one Nigerian,” Obi said. The attack occurred in Uduere community, Ughelli North Local Government Area of Delta State, during a political gathering involving Omo-Agege, the NDC senatorial candidate for Delta Central. Omo-Agege had alleged that the attackers repeatedly called his name and threatened to kill him during the incident. He said he escaped through the intervention of his security escorts. Following the violence, the Delta State Government imposed a 12-hour curfew in Ughelli North Local Government Area to prevent further breakdown of law and order. The Minister of Aviation and Aerospace Development, Festus Keyamo, also condemned the political violence, warning that the “Rig and Die” slogan was contributing to tension in the state. He called on those promoting the slogan to publicly withdraw it and apologise.
